tagline: Morocco's Atlantic resort and surf coast — Agadir marina to Essaouira's UNESCO medina port, a ~90 nm coastal run today driven, ripe for a clean Quanta-LR sea line.
summary: Morocco's central Atlantic coast pairs Agadir — a planned resort city with a modern marina and Morocco's leading beach-tourism volume — with Essaouira, the UNESCO-listed walled medina and windsurf capital ~90 nm north, plus the surf-and-resort belt of Taghazout Bay between them. Today the coast is connected by road; sea movement is limited to fishing fleets and marina day-boats. Demand is tourism- and resort-led, with a strong national push (Vision 2030, World Cup 2030 co-hosting) driving coastal infrastructure investment. A foiling-electric layer fits the resort-transfer and coastal-corridor pattern; the open Atlantic swell makes Quanta-LR's range and stability the right tool for the Agadir<->Essaouira line, while Pioneer II serves Agadir-bay and Taghazout transfers. This market also anchors a North-Africa entry point for a demand-platform partner.

competitive_landscape: Today: road transfers, fishing fleets, marina day-boats; no clean fast-passenger coastal service.
seasonality: Year-round mild climate; Atlantic swell and Essaouira wind make a stable foiling hull a comfort/safety advantage.
regulatory_note: Agadir and Essaouira are commercial ports under ANP; marina operations under SAPST/marina concessionaires.
